question.leadin: Answer the following questions related to the Seven Years' War.
question.text: The American theater of the Seven Years' War is commonly known by this name, which references the two main enemies that the British colonists fought during the war.
question.clue: Dissatisfaction with the result of this war led to Pontiac's Rebellion.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about early colonization of the Americas.
swap.text: This was the first permanent English settlement in North America, founded in 1607. It nearly succumbed to famine in its early years, but was kept afloat by the leadership of John Smith and Lord De La Warr.
swap.clue: Residents of this city practiced cannibalism during the "starving time".

question.leadin: The war saw the British under Anson attacking the Manila Galleon, after which he circumnavigated the globe.
question.text: Identify this war that saw the battles at Porto Bello and Cartagena that was sparked by the Spanish seizure of its namesake's ship, Rebecca.
question.clue: Seeing an unsuccessful amphibious assault on Cartagena de Indias, the incident that sparked this war involved the boarding of the ship Rebecca.

swap.leadin: Give the following about labor practices in 19th century America.
swap.text: Many Europeans migrated to the Americas by becoming this type of laborer, in which they exchanged several years of labor for their passage and were guaranteed their freedom at the end of the contract.
swap.answerHtml: indentured servants (accept word forms, like indentured servitude; prompt on servant)
swap.clue: The book's second chapter argues that the "color line" was created to pacify these people by distinguishing them from slaves. These servants worked without pay for a set amount of time.

question.text: Mary Beth Norton argued that this event should be understood within the context of King William's War. This 1690s event led to the deaths of twenty people who allegedly worked with the devil.
question.clue: The tract Wonders of the Invisible World was written to defend its author, Cotton Mather, for his participation in these events.

swap.text: This parliamentary act reinforced mercantilist theory by allowing British colonists to only import goods directly from England and only export goods on British ships.
swap.clue: Repealed officially in 1849, they were accompanied by the Staple Act and targeted items subject to "enumeration."

question.leadin: Sassacus led one side in this war.
question.text: Name this war, during which colonists under John Mason killed hundreds of Narragansetts during the Mystic Massacre.
question.clue: The Mohawks effectively ended this war after they killed the Grand Sachem Sassacus as a sign of goodwill to the English colonists.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about colonial American rebellions.
swap.text: This member of the House of Burgesses began a rebellion by raiding the land of neighboring Doeg Indians. He died of dysentery soon after issuing a "Declaration of the People" criticizing his colony's administration.
swap.clue: This man called an Assembly to stamp out corruption and raise tobacco prices.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Native American prophets.
question.text: The prophet Neolin's anti-materialistic messages directly influenced this chieftain, who revolted against Jeffrey Amherst's Indian policies.
question.clue: A reward for this man's death was announced by Jeffrey Amherst.

swap.leadin: Name these conflicts between Native Americans and European settlers.
swap.text: In 1763, this Ottowa chief led an alliance of midwestern tribes against British forts. His victory at the Battle of Bloody Run allowed him to lay siege to Detroit.
swap.clue: Before this war, the practice of gift-giving was ended by Jeffery Amherst, who later authorized the use of smallpox-infected blankets as bioweapons.

question.leadin: Answer the following about U.S. relations with Native Americans.
question.text: Over a century earlier, this group of western Pennsylvanian frontiersmen got so furious in the face of Pontiac's rebellion that they started massacring the peaceful Susquehannock Indians.
question.clue: Their first fight was prompted by Matthew Smith's reconnaissance, and Asher Clayton and Lazarus Stewart led their two companies, which were started by Colonel Reverend John Elder.

swap.leadin: Name these men important in Colonial Virginia.
swap.text: A onetime captive of the Turks, this principal founder of was saved by Pocahontas after he was captured by the Powhatan Confederacy
swap.clue: The Tidewater and Pamunkey tribes captured this man in their hunting raids and their 'emperor' let him live.

question.leadin: At the 1784 Christmas Conference, this denomination officially took up an anti-slavery stance.
question.text: Name this denomination whose "African Episcopal" offshoot, established by Richard Allen and Absalom Jones, is the oldest Protestant denomination founded by African-Americans.
question.answerHtml: Methodism [or Wesleyan Church; or Methodist Episcopal Church; or African Methodist Episcopal Church; prompt on AME Church]
question.clue: "Connexions," or offshoots, of this movement included the Kilhamites.

swap.text: As an apprentice, Benjamin Franklin printed the New-England Courant newspaper, which featured this female persona of his giving humorous accounts of colonial life.
swap.clue: Benjamin Franklin, who wrote Poor Richard's Almanack, had earlier written in the New England Courant under this pseudonym. 14 letters published in 1722 were attributed to Franklin under this pseudonym.

question.leadin: During this war, raiders under Jean-Baptiste Hertel de Rouville ("air-TELL duh roo-VEEL") attacked English forces in Deerfield, Massachusetts, killing four dozen colonists.
question.text: Name this war named after an English monarch, the American theater of the War of Spanish Succession. During this war, the Wabanaki stopped New England from expanding into Acadia.
question.answerHtml: Queen Anne’s War [or Third Indian War; or Second Intercolonial War]
question.clue: During this war, British forces made three attempts, the last of which was successful, to capture the Acadian capital of Port Royal, defended by the Wabanaki Confederacy and France.

swap.leadin: This administrative unit included all the land from New Jersey to Maine.
swap.text: Name this short-lived North American government with which Charles II tried to rein in some of his colonies. It began with the revocation of Massachusetts's commercial charter.
swap.clue: Its first president later became chief justice of New York, and sentenced Jacob Leisler to death for treason.

question.leadin: The sachem ("SAY-chum") White Eyes negotiated a 1778 treaty named after this fort that allied the Lenape ("luh-NAH-pay") with the U.S.
question.text: Name this fort, which was the site of a siege during Pontiac's War where Henry Bouquet ("boo-KAY") employed smallpox blankets. This fort was built following the Forbes Expedition, during which nearby Fort Duquesne ("dew-KANE") was razed.
question.clue: One of the central events of the Rebellion was the siege of this fort, whose commander attempted to infect the Indians with smallpox. It was built near the site of the old Fort Duquesne in 1759.

swap.leadin: Name these things about James Oglethorpe's role in the War of Jenkins' Ear.
swap.text: Oglethorpe's first action was to lead an unsuccessful siege of this Spanish city. It was founded in 1565 by Pedro Menendez, making it the oldest continuously occupied site settled by Europeans in the Americas.
swap.clue: Coquina rock was used to build a bastioned fortress protecting this city, the Castillo de San Marcos, that replaced a cedar-log fort burned by Sir Francis Drake in 1586.

question.text: This governor tried to regulate trade with tribes south of the James River, particularly the Saponi and Tutelo, in 1714 by creating Fort Christanna and the Virginia Indian Company, but William Byrd saw this quashed by the Lords of Trade in 1718.
question.clue: This royal governor of colonial Virginia sent the Knights of the Golden Horseshoe, a 1716 expedition to the Blue Ridge Mountains. He also set up the mining settlement Germanna for, you guessed it, German immigrants.

swap.text: Further anti-Andros activity could be seen in New York, where this German-born colonist led a 1689 revolt which deposed Andros' deputy Francis Nicholson. He was eventually executed in 1691 for treason.
swap.clue: The major accomplishment of his two-year-long regime was calling for an attack on Quebec in the first independent congress of the North American colonies.
